title: Reversion Basics
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/0/tit: Price is like a rubber band
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/0/bod: **Mean reversion** means that when price stretches far from its **average**, it's likely to snap back toward it, like an overstretched rubber band. You'll see this behavior most in a **ranging market**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/1/tit: How do we measure the mean?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/1/bod: Traders usually use a **moving average** like the SMA 20 as the mean. When price is far **below** it, a reversion trader looks to buy. When it's far **above**, they look to sell. The first target is **the average itself**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/1/tip: On this lesson's short charts we use the SMA 10, so the line shows up from the start of the chart.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/2/pro: What's the core idea of a mean reversion strategy?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/2/opt: Price that's stretched too far from the mean will likely head back toward it
Price that's moved away from the mean always keeps drifting further
You should always trade in the direction of the last candle
A moving average predicts the next high and low exactly
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/2/exp: Mean reversion bets that extreme moves inside a range get corrected. That's a probability, not a certainty.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/3/pro: The market is ranging, and price hit the range bottom with a hammer, more than 30 pips below the mean. What does a reversion trader do?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/3/exp: In a range, being far from the mean plus a long lower wick makes a bounce back toward the mean (around 1.0850) more likely. It's not certain, so you need a stop loss below the hammer's low.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/4/sta: Mean reversion strategies work best in strong trends.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/4/exp: In a strong trend, price can stay far from the mean for ages, and cheap can get cheaper. This strategy belongs mostly in ranging markets.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/5/bod: **Trend following** says what's strong gets stronger, so it buys strength. **Mean reversion** says extreme moves get corrected, so in a range it buys weakness and sells strength. Each one works in its own conditions.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/5/tip: Before every trade, ask yourself: is the market trending right now, or ranging?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/6/pai: Buying weakness and selling strength in a range
Price swinging between a flat top and bottom
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/7/sen: When price has dropped far below the mean, a reversion trader looks to ___, and the first target is usually the ___ itself.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l1/steps/7/exp: In a range, price that's stretched to the downside has a chance to bounce back up. So you buy, aiming for price to reach the mean again.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/0/bod: In a **ranging market**, price bounces up and down between a roughly flat **top** and **bottom**. The highs and lows line up, the **moving average stays flat** and price keeps crossing from one side of it to the other.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/1/bod: In an **uptrend**, price makes **higher highs and higher lows**, the average **slopes**, and price stays on one side of it most of the time. Selling above the average here means standing in front of the current.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/2/pro: Is this market ranging or trending?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/2/exp: Highs keep landing around 3045 and lows around 2955, and the average is almost flat. The market is ranging.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/3/exp: Every high and every low is lower than the one before, and the average slopes down. Buying below the average here would have been fighting the trend.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/4/sta: In a ranging market, the moving average is usually flat and price crosses it again and again.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/4/exp: When buyers and sellers are about evenly matched, the average has no real direction and price swings back and forth around it.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/5/bod: Mean reversion only has an edge in a **range**. In a **trend**, price that looks cheap can get cheaper. So step one of every reversion trade is **figuring out the market type**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/5/tip: A simple clue: if price has stayed on one side of the average for many candles, you probably have a trend, not a range.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/6/pro: Which sign points more to a ranging market?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/6/opt: A flat average with highs and lows at the same levels
Higher highs and higher lows one after another
Price has stayed above the average for 20 candles
Long candles in a row, all in one direction
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/6/exp: Matching highs and lows with a flat average means the market has no direction. The other options are signs of a trend.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/7/sen: In a range, price bounces up from ___ (the range bottom) and turns down from ___ (the range top).
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/7/exp: The lower edge of the range is support (buyers step in) and the upper edge is resistance (sellers step in).
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/8/pro: In a strong uptrend, a trader sold every time price rose above the average and took loss after loss. What's the main mistake?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/8/opt: Running a range strategy in a trending market
The stop loss was too far away
Should have used a lower timeframe
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l2/steps/8/exp: In an uptrend, price above the average is normal, not extreme. Figure out the market type first, then pick your strategy.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/0/bod: You can measure how far price is from the mean in **pips**, **percent** or **standard deviations**. The more stretched price is, the more likely a snap back in a range. But remember: **stretched can get even more stretched**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/1/pro: The EUR/USD SMA 20 is at 1.0850 and price is at 1.0790. How many pips below the mean is price?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/1/exp: 1.0850 − 1.0790 = 0.0060. On EUR/USD every 0.0001 is one pip, so that's 60 pips.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/2/pro: Bitcoin's SMA 20 is $60,000 and price has dropped to $57,000. What percent below the mean is price?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/2/exp: The gap is $3,000, and 3,000 ÷ 60,000 = 0.05, so 5% below the mean.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/3/bod: **Standard deviation** shows how far price usually swings around its mean. A move of **2 standard deviations** is usually considered unusual. That same idea is the basis of **Bollinger Bands**, which you'll meet in the next unit.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/3/tip: Markets have fat tails: really big moves happen more often than simple statistics predict.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/4/pro: Tap the candle that closed furthest below the mean.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/4/exp: After a sharp drop, this candle closed about $1,600 below the mean, the most stretched point on the chart. Look how price headed back toward the mean afterward.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/5/sta: When price moves 2 standard deviations from the mean, it always turns back right away.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/5/exp: A big stretch only makes a snap back more likely in a range. In a trend, or after major news, price can stay stretched for a long time.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/6/pro: GBP/USD is ranging, and price has pushed more than 30 pips above the mean with a shooting star. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/6/exp: Price is near the range top and far from the mean, and the long upper wick shows buyers couldn't hold it up. A move back toward the mean (around 1.2700) is more likely, but not certain.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/7/pro: Put the steps of a mean reversion trade in order.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/7/ite: Make sure the market is ranging
Wait for price to stretch from the mean
Put your stop beyond the high or low
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/7/exp: First the market type, then the distance from the mean, then confirmation of the reversal. Your stop is set before you enter, and the natural target is the mean itself.
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/8/pro: Look at these conditions. Which plan makes the most sense?
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/8/opt: Buy with a stop below the low and the mean as target
Sell, because price is going down
Buy with no stop, since price will definitely bounce
Wait for price to break the range top, then buy
lessons/mean-reversion-u1-l3/steps/8/exp: All the signs line up: a range, a big stretch and a reversal candle. But nothing is certain, so a stop below the low is a must.
